items.title: Run the CLI through a symlinked path (npm .bin link, node_modules/<pkg> under pnpm)
body: npm installs `bin` as a symlink `node_modules/.bin/houserules -> ../houserules/bin/houserules.mjs`. Node resolves `import.meta.url` through the symlink but keeps `process.argv[1]` as the `.bin` path, so the entry guard in `bin/houserules.mjs` never matches and the CLI exits 0 without output.

Fix: compare against `realpathSync(process.argv[1])` in the guard; apply the same idiom in `template/tools/kb.mjs` and `template/tools/backlog.mjs`. Regression test: run the bin through a symlink and expect the manifest.
Verified live on 2026-08-31 with `npm exec --package=git+file://<clone> -- houserules files`: 0 lines, exit 0; the direct path prints the manifest.

Probe of 2026-09-01 under pnpm 11.18.0 (`pnpm add --save-exact git+file://<clone>` in a scratch project): `pnpm exec houserules files` and `pnpm dlx git+file://<clone> files` print the manifest, because pnpm's bin shim execs the real path under `node_modules/.pnpm/`; `node node_modules/houserules/bin/houserules.mjs files` through the package symlink prints nothing and exits 0. The defect is independent of the package manager.

items.title: Report invalid JSON in knowledge and backlog files as a usage error
body: `loadBase` and `loadBacklog` let `JSON.parse` errors escape as stack traces (`SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1`); `tools/kb.sh render` inside `init` then dies with the raw trace.

Fix: `readJson` raises a `UsageError` that names the file and the parse message, as `audit --report` already does for a malformed report. `init` keeps failing with a non-zero exit; the init test `lets a render failure on broken project data propagate as a real error` stays valid.

items.title: Port process.evals-rerun with its co-change check and evals record from tag-pilot
body: tag-pilot `fc3241b` (2026-08-31) adds the rule `process.evals-rerun`: re-run every `.claude/evals/` scenario whenever the implementer or task-reviewer template or a scenario changes; a `co-change` check fails the audit until `.claude/evals/record.json` changes with them; the record keys runs by the templates' git blob ids. The orchestrating skill gains a 'Template evaluation' procedure and the branch reviewer compares the record's blob ids with HEAD.

Blocked until PR #42 is merged (owner instruction). Then port it to `template/` (knowledge entry, orchestrating skill bullet, branch-reviewer check, and the `kb.mjs` co-change lines if the drift holds them) and diff the remaining drift.

items.title: Switch this repository to pnpm and set the workspace up like tag-pilot
body: Owner ruling of 2026-09-01 (docs/design.md §5.7): use pnpm only, never npm or npx.

Scope: exact `node` and `pnpm` pins in `mise.toml` written by `mise use`; `pnpm-lock.yaml` replaces `package-lock.json`; `pnpm-workspace.yaml` for the pnpm settings; the mise tasks `setup`, `test`, `lint`, and `audit` as in tag-pilot; README, knowledge entries, and the development commands name pnpm. `template/` stays dependency-free.
The batch 2 spec fixes the file list and settles the commitlint commit-msg hook.

items.title: Capture the render child's stderr in init instead of inheriting it
body: `install` in `bin/houserules.mjs` spawns `tools/kb.mjs render` with an inherited stderr, so the init test on broken project data prints one usage-error line into the suite output (tests/init.test.mjs, 'lets a render failure on broken project data propagate as a real error').
Fix: spawn with `stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe']` and put the child's stderr into the thrown error; the test asserts the message and the suite output stays silent.
Source: task 3 re-review and the batch 2 branch review (2026-09-01).

items.title: Enforce the commit body line limit in the commits check
body: The `commits` check of `tools/kb.sh audit` tests the subject pattern and `body_absent` only; two controller commits with 190- and 227-character body lines passed the batch 2 audits as '9 commits checked'. Only the commit-msg hook catches it, for commits made after it was installed.

Fix: add the optional key `body_line_max` (integer, minimum 1) to `$defs.check` in `knowledge/schema.json` and `template/knowledge/schema.json`; in the `commits` runner of `template/tools/kb.mjs`, fail a commit with a body line longer than the limit; regression tests for 100 and 101 characters and a `checkShape` case; `update --dir .`.

Ruled 2026-09-01 (docs/design.md §5.8): the same task sets `body_line_max: 100` on `process.conventional-commits` in `knowledge/process.json` and `template/knowledge/process.json`. Source: batch 2 branch review, violated_rules.

items.title: Agent template and deliverables refinements from the batch 2 retrospective
body: Deliverables schema (`template/.claude/schemas/deliverables.json` and the root copy): add an optional integer `exit` to `$defs.run`; the implementer template's Report section names it for every run whose exit code is evidence, and `output` stays verbatim (batch 2: exit codes were written into `output` as prose).

Implementer template `coverage`: 'one measure per target whenever the project has a coverage gate and the full suite ran, so the batch keeps a baseline; null only when the suite did not run' (batch 2 task 1 left it null and a fix round repaired it).

Orchestrating skill, dispatch protocol: a brief names no version number for a tool, action, or package (security-hygiene.exact-pins); it names the verification the implementer runs and shows placeholders such as `jdx/mise-action@<current major>` (batch 2 task 1 brief carried a stale `@v2`).
Source: batch 2 branch review, template_defects 2-4.

items.title: Audit report-field checks over a workspace of task reports
body: A branch has no single report, so the four report-field rows (deliverables-json, knowledge-first, dependency-vetting, verify-current-docs) come back `skipped` from `tools/kb.sh audit` and the branch reviewer judges them by hand from the task reports.

Fix: accept `--report` more than once, or add `--workspace <dir>` that reads every `task-*-report.json`; a report-field check passes when every report whose changed files trigger it sets the field, and names the offending report otherwise. Source: batch 2 branch review, template_defects 5.

items.title: Diff the audit range from the merge base
body: `changedFiles` in `template/tools/kb.mjs` diffs `base..head`, so the pull-request audit (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) sees unrelated files when main moves after the branch was cut. Inherited from tag-pilot's knowledge.yml.

Fix: `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR --merge-base <base> <head>` for the files, `git log <base>..<head>` for the commits; a test with a moved base. Source: batch 2 branch review, recommendations.

items.title: Report an unreadable .houserules.json as a usage error
body: `install` parses the stamp with raw `JSON.parse(readFileSync(markerPath))`; an unreadable `.houserules.json` escapes as a SyntaxError stack trace. `tests/init.test.mjs` (the test "propagates an unreadable marker, which is a defect and not a usage error") pins the current behavior until this item.

Fix: reuse `readJson` from `template/tools/lib/json-store.mjs` (it raises `UsageError` with `<path>: invalid JSON (...)`; the bin already imports from that module) and rewrite the pinning test the way HR-005 rewrote its predecessor.
Source: batch 3 task 1 review (2026-09-01); the branch review filed the missing item as its critical finding.

items.title: Carry the git stderr in the no-merge-base usage error
body: `gitDiff` in `template/tools/kb.mjs` reports every `git diff` failure as `no merge base between "<base>" and "<head>"` and discards the child stderr, so a different failure (a missing object in a shallow clone, repository corruption) is mislabeled and its diagnostic lost.
Fix: pipe the child stderr and include it in the `UsageError`, or use the no-merge-base text only when the stderr indicates it; sync the root copy; one test.
Deferred from batch 3 with the branch review’s reason: `rev` pre-validates both refs, so the remaining failure modes are exotic. Source: batch 3 branch review, minor 2 (2026-09-01).

items.title: Dispatch-protocol bullets: a brief carries the spec, a dispatch carries changed templates
body: Two additions to the orchestrating skill’s dispatch protocol (`template/.claude/skills/orchestrating/SKILL.md`, kit-owned, then `update --dir .`): a brief names every test and gate its spec task lists, verbatim or by pointer (batch 3 task 3’s brief dropped the seed-checkBase test and the gap cost a review round); when a batch edits an agent template, the dispatch message carries the changed instruction verbatim, because templates load at session start (batch 3’s branch review ran on the pre-branch template).
Consider seeding `process.brief-carries-the-spec` (added to the root knowledge at the batch 3 close) into `template/knowledge/process.json` in the same task.
Source: batch 3 branch review, template_defects 1 and 3 (2026-09-01).

items.title: A migration skill: move a pre-existing codebase’s knowledge into the houserules style
body: Owner request of 2026-09-01: when houserules is installed into a codebase that already has knowledge (CLAUDE.md prose, docs, wikis, comments, ad-hoc rules files), a skill in the payload explains how to migrate it: inventory the sources, split rule/invariant/gotcha/procedure/decision/history, write entries per the schema (summary is the rule, ≤160; body why/how/exceptions; source with date and by; verify paths; check where deterministic), extend areas, park the leftovers, delete the migrated originals, and gate with tools/kb.sh check plus render.

Shape to design in the batch spec: a kit-owned skill (template/.claude/skills/, overwritten by update) that the README’s install-to-existing section points to; likely with a worked example and the knowledge-base.* rules by pointer.
Candidate for batch 5 with its own spec gate.

items.title: Read settings.json through readJson in the bin
body: `mergeSettings` in `bin/houserules.mjs` still parses `.claude/settings.json` by hand and wraps the failure as `not readable JSON (...)`, a second wording for the failure class the stamp path now reports as `invalid JSON` through `readJson`.

Fix: `settings = readJson(path)` and drop the catch; the existing test asserts exit 2 and the file name only. Decide the one semantic change: an unreadable (not just invalid) settings.json then propagates as a plain Error, like the stamp.
Source: batch 4 task 1 review, minor (2026-09-01); deferred out of HR-010 because of that semantics decision.
